solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: “Scandalous!”, fumes Hal, distraught (8)

indicatorNotes.distraught: distraught means driven to distraction, so the letters are thrown into disorder

annotation.surface: Hal is furious, fuming and crying out that something is a scandal.
annotation.walkthrough: The exclamation at the front is the definition; the fuming Hal who utters it supplies every letter.
annotation.definitionFit: Something scandalous is shameful: it brings disgrace.

entries.clue: Port’s house nothing outstanding? (8)

blocks.note: HO is the standard abbreviation for house
a lulu is an outstanding thing or person

annotation.surface: A question about a port town whose houses are all rather ordinary.
annotation.walkthrough: The ’s is 'is': Port is house + nothing + outstanding. Read the wordplay as 'no lulu', nothing outstanding, which is what makes the surface question sound dismissive.
annotation.definitionFit: Honolulu, capital of Hawaii, is a major Pacific port.

entries.clue: Change in objectives, since promise has been broken (7,5)

indicatorNotes.has been broken: a broken promise is one smashed apart, so its letters are rearranged

annotation.surface: Someone explains that plans have changed because a promise was not kept.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface gives a plausible reason for changing aims; in fact 'since promise' is the raw material, broken up.
annotation.definitionFit: Mission creep is the gradual expansion of a project's objectives beyond what was first set.

entries.clue: Versatile employee, in truth corporation receiving nothing (8)

indicatorNotes.receiving: the corporation takes in the nothing, which sits against its front

blocks.note: a corporation is jocular British slang for a large belly, a tum

annotation.surface: A remark about a jack-of-all-trades working for a truthful company.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Corporation' sounds like business, which suits the employee; here it is the old joke meaning a pot belly, TUM.
annotation.definitionFit: A factotum is an employee who does all kinds of work.

entries.clue: Dropping round with Carol (7)

blocks.note: a lap is one round of a track

annotation.surface: Something falling round in company with a woman called Carol.
annotation.walkthrough: Carol takes a capital to pose as a name; it is the verb, to sing joyfully.
annotation.definitionFit: Lapsing means dropping away, as a subscription or standard lapses.

entries.clue: Greeting son in the manner of mother upset (6)

indicatorNotes.upset: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so MA reads upwards

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for son
à la, borrowed French for 'in the style of'

annotation.surface: A son greets someone just as his upset mother would.
annotation.walkthrough: Upset seems to describe the mother's mood; it is the instruction to turn MA over.
annotation.definitionFit: A borrowed word: the Arabic salutation meaning 'peace', also the low bow that goes with it.

entries.clue: Too wrapped up in Apollo’s launch (4)

indicatorNotes.wrapped: the answer is wrapped inside the following words
indicatorNotes.up: in a down clue, up means read upwards
indicatorNotes.in: the answer sits in the words that follow

annotation.surface: Someone is too absorbed in watching the Apollo rocket lift off.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer runs backwards across the break between the two words, which makes it easy to miss.
annotation.definitionFit: Also and too both mean in addition.

entries.clue: Religious leader seen in Welsh town (8)

annotation.surface: A cleric is spotted in a town in Wales.
annotation.walkthrough: HOLYHEAD is a port town on Anglesey in north Wales, where ferries leave for Ireland.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: the ferry port on Anglesey is one example of a Welsh town.

entries.clue: A mafioso touring capitals coming across large resort (8)

indicatorNotes.touring: to tour is to go round, so CAPO goes round the rest
indicatorNotes.coming across: UC comes across, spanning, the L

blocks.note: the A stays as it is
a capo is a Mafia boss
UC stands for upper case, capital letters
L = large, as on clothing labels

annotation.surface: A gangster travels round the capitals and turns up at a big holiday resort.
annotation.walkthrough: Upper case is the printer's term for capital letters. Two containers nest here, so work from the inside out.
annotation.definitionFit: Acapulco is a resort on Mexico's Pacific coast.

entries.clue: Foreigners, not at first following locals (4)

indicatorNotes.not at first: the first letter is taken away

blocks.note: Finns, people from Finland, stand for foreigners generally
F = following, as in page references; this is the letter removed

annotation.surface: Foreigners arrive after the local people, and not at the start.
annotation.walkthrough: In Britain a local is a nearby pub, which is how 'locals' defines INNS; the local people of the surface are a decoy.
annotation.definitionFit: A local is one's neighbourhood pub, and inns are pubs.

entries.clue: Settled, lives and works OK (12)

blocks.note: a bird that has settled has sat

annotation.surface: A verdict that a settled life and job are fine.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lives and works' sounds like a description of someone's circumstances; each word is a separate piece.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both describe something good enough, meeting the standard without excelling.

entries.clue: First sample maybe that’s hooked to second steroid (12)

indicatorNotes.that’s hooked: the first sample has hooked, caught up inside it, the following letters

blocks.note: a tester is a sample, as of perfume in a shop

annotation.surface: A lab's first specimen is linked to a second steroid, as in a doping case.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads like a doping story; 'first' belongs with the sample, but it comes last in the answer. 'To' is used as itself.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: the male sex hormone belongs to the steroid family, and is the one athletes are tested for.

entries.clue: Countries coming together in defeat become exhausted (3,3)

indicatorNotes.in: 'in defeat' means placed inside the word for defeat, so UN sits within ROUT

blocks.note: a rout is a heavy defeat
the United Nations, countries joined together

annotation.surface: Allied nations united in a defeat grow tired.
annotation.walkthrough: RUN OUT is also a cricket dismissal, which suits the defeat of the surface.
annotation.definitionFit: A phrasal-verb synonym: supplies are used up, exhausted, when there are none left.

entries.clue: Another so-called “man” in need of flipping energy drink! (8)

indicatorNotes.in need of flipping: the word MAN is to be flipped round

annotation.surface: A man in need of an energy drink.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Energy drink' is a single thing in the surface; split it into E and SAKE.
annotation.definitionFit: A namesake is another person called by the same name.

entries.clue: Result of inaccurate approach (7)

blocks.note: a guess that is out is inaccurate

annotation.surface: What happens when your approach is wrong.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Inaccurate approach' looks like one idea; it is two pieces, OUT and COME.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the outcome of an event is what comes out of it, its result.

entries.clue: Refuse to accept company no longer sanctioned (8)

blocks.note: ICI, Imperial Chemical Industries, a British company that no longer exists

annotation.surface: An order to refuse dealings with a company that has been sanctioned.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' reads as a verb; it is the noun, rubbish. ICI was a British chemicals giant taken over in 2008.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an official figure or statement carries the approval of authority, which is what sanctioned means.

entries.clue: Face down in trailer in protective garment (7)

indicatorNotes.in: 'in trailer' means placed inside the word for trailer, so PRONE sits within AD

blocks.note: a trailer advertises a film, so it is an ad

annotation.surface: Someone lies face down in a caravan, wearing protective clothing.
annotation.walkthrough: The trailer is not a caravan but a film preview, AD.
annotation.definitionFit: Aproned means wearing an apron, a protective garment.

entries.clue: Mournful, mean fellow (8)

blocks.note: to mean to do something is to plan it

annotation.surface: A sad, miserly man.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Mean' looks like the adjective for stingy; it is the verb, to intend.
annotation.definitionFit: Plangent describes a loud, mournful sound.

entries.clue: Spirit driver away from Escort, one damaged by cracks (8)

indicatorNotes.damaged: the letters of ESCORT I are damaged, rearranged
indicatorNotes.cracks: X cracks, breaks into, the rearranged letters

blocks.note: by as in multiplication, three by four, written X

annotation.surface: An exorcist steers clear of a Ford Escort that has a damaged, cracked windscreen.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition 'Spirit driver away' runs straight on into 'from Escort'; 'from' is the link. 'By' is the times sign X.
annotation.definitionFit: An exorcist drives evil spirits away.

entries.clue: Top of tree was shaking (7)

annotation.surface: The top of a tree swayed in the wind.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Top of tree' is not the treetop; Top is a garment, and a sweater is a top.
annotation.definitionFit: A sweater is a top, a garment for the upper body.

entries.clue: Anticipated quartet being unfamiliar to audience (8)

indicatorNotes.to audience: what the audience hears, not how it is written

annotation.surface: A string quartet is expected to be new to its listeners.
annotation.walkthrough: Both pieces are sound-alikes: FOUR NEW heard as FORE KNEW.
annotation.definitionFit: To foreknow is to know in advance, to anticipate.

entries.clue: Idiot can put up with losing footing (6)

indicatorNotes.put up: in a down clue, put up means turned upwards
indicatorNotes.losing footing: the foot, the last letter, is lost

annotation.surface: A fool can tolerate losing his balance.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Put up with' reads as tolerate; split it so 'put up' reverses TIN and 'with' is the fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both are mild, informal names for a foolish person.

entries.clue: To the French, all the same Republican cause? (6)

blocks.note: tho', a short spelling of though, all the same

annotation.surface: To the French, it seems, every Republican cause looks alike.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the loose definition: an author is the one who causes something to exist.
annotation.definitionFit: An extended sense: beyond writers, the word covers whoever originates anything, as 'the author of his own misfortune'.

entries.clue: CPGB regret a mix-up with a candidate from outside (12)

indicatorNotes.mix-up: a mix-up is a muddle, and muddled letters no longer keep their order

blocks.note: the second A joins the fodder

annotation.surface: The Communist Party of Great Britain regrets a muddle over an outsider candidate.
annotation.walkthrough: CPGB is the Communist Party of Great Britain, which makes the surface sound like a political news item.
annotation.definitionFit: A carpetbagger is a politician who stands in a place where they have no local connections.

entries.clue: The luxury of having court documents read out (4)

indicatorNotes.read out: read out means spoken, so we want the sound

annotation.surface: A lawyer's fancy for having legal papers read aloud.
annotation.walkthrough: The Ritz is a famously luxurious London hotel, a byword for luxury as in 'putting on the Ritz'; the definition keeps its 'The'.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by metonymy: the grand hotel's name has become shorthand for opulence, as in 'putting on the Ritz'.

entries.clue: Piece dug out by club recalled timeless old poet (4)

indicatorNotes.timeless: 'less' means without, so the word goes without its T for time

blocks.note: a divot is turf cut out by a golf club
T = time; this is the letter removed

annotation.surface: A club brings back a fragment of an ancient poet unearthed in a dig.
annotation.walkthrough: The club is a golf club, not a society; the chunk it digs up is a divot.
annotation.definitionFit: Ovid was a Roman poet of the first century BC.

entries.clue: At A&E having ingested drug (8)

indicatorNotes.having ingested: A and E swallow the drug between them

blocks.note: A and E, taken as the two letters
a statin is a cholesterol-lowering drug

annotation.surface: A patient in the emergency department after swallowing drugs.
annotation.walkthrough: 'At' looks like a link word; it is the chemical symbol for astatine. A&E is the British hospital emergency department.
annotation.definitionFit: A crossword-only sense: the element's chemical symbol stands in for its name, so 'At' is the radioactive halogen.

entries.clue: Goes back on right to return fare (8)

indicatorNotes.to return: to return is to come back, so the letters come back in reverse order

blocks.note: RT is the abbreviation for right

annotation.surface: Someone goes back on their right to a refund of the fare.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Goes back on' sounds like reneging, and 'return fare' like a ticket; both phrases must be split.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an army withdrawing from a position goes back, and the third-person form matches 'Goes'.
